:::{#exr-hyperplane-origin-practice}
#### Describing a line in $\reals^2$ by a point and a vector

Part 2 of @thm-hyperplane-origin says that a [hyperplane](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-hyperplane) in $\reals^2$
is a line $\cb{\vx_0 + t\,\vecf{v} : t \in \reals}$ for a point $\vx_0$ and a nonzero vector $\vecf{v}$.
Let $\mathcal{H} = \cb{\vx \in \reals^2 : 2 x_1 + x_2 - 4 = 0}$.

Find a point $\vx_0$ and a nonzero vector $\vecf{v}$ with $\mathcal{H} = \cb{\vx_0 + t\,\vecf{v} : t \in \reals}$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Find one point of $\mathcal{H}$ by setting $x_2 = 0$, and take $\vecf{v} = (-w_2, w_1)$ as in @exm-hyperplane-origin.

:::
